answer: Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the ferrous checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. The voyage graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the yarrow audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 4 times its size, so a group of 47 keys loses far more than 47 single identities would. That is 13 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
